items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Muriel Zuckerman, the secretary of Benny Goodman, who befriended my wife then. And they became good friends, and I needed somebody, and she offered.

ctx.x: Because Benny Goodman had tried to get the working permit for me here, and it was much harder than… I don’t know. It’s still hard now to, for somebody to come and work in the States. We had to be, we had to have a sponsor, affidavit. And you know who wound up being my affidavit? Muriel Zuckerman, the secretary of Benny Goodman, who befriended my wife then. And they became good friends, and I needed somebody, and she offered. That was beautiful, because signing an affidavit is accepting to see the person who be…
owing money or losing money, she would have had to see that I got back to Belgium. And which I didn’t. [laughs] I was, I worked [inaudible]. But I made it, of course. [laughs]
